rektion: jdn./etw./sich aus etw. (Dat.) / von etw. (Dat.) befreien
meaning_en: to free, to release, to rescue (from)
definition_de: jdn. oder etwas aus einer Gefangenschaft oder einer engen, gefährlichen Lage holen; auch: von etwas Lästigem frei machen (sich von Schulden befreien; von der Steuer befreit sein)
example_de: Der Taucher schnitt das alte Fischernetz auf und befreite die Meeresschildkröte.
example_en: The diver cut open the old fishing net and freed the sea turtle.
visual_idea: Collocation 'ein Tier aus einem Netz befreien': the result state shows the turtle swimming away with flippers spread while the diver still holds the cut net, so trapped-then-free is visible in one frame. Rejected: a bird leaving an open cage (reads as 'freilassen') and a cat in a tree (reads as 'retten'). The change from trapped to free is the meaning, so a first+last-frame video starts with the turtle tangled in the net.
image_prompt: underwater view in clear turquoise sea, sunlight rays falling from above, sandy bottom; on the left a diver in a black wetsuit with yellow fins holds a cut-open old green fishing net in one hand; on the right a large green sea turtle swims freely away from him, its front flippers spread wide, nothing on its body, small bubbles rising
negative_prompt: text, letters, watermark, signature, caption, blurry, extra fingers, deformed hands, cluttered background, multiple panels
video_start_prompt: underwater view in clear turquoise sea, sunlight rays falling from above, sandy bottom; on the left a diver in a black wetsuit with yellow fins reaches forward with a small knife; on the right a large green sea turtle is tightly wrapped in an old green fishing net, its flippers tangled and pressed against its shell
video_prompt: underwater, static camera: a diver in a black wetsuit with yellow fins carefully cuts an old green fishing net wrapped around a large green sea turtle; the net falls open, the diver pulls it away and holds it, and the turtle spreads its flippers and slowly swims away free
